_meta.indication: Treatment of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (CTCL) in patients who have received at least one prior systemic therapy

pivotal_trials.trial_name: GPI-04-0001 (Study 1), the pivotal single-arm phase II study
pivotal_trials.design: International, multicenter, single-arm, single-agent open-label study
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with confirmed CTCL after failure of at least 1 prior systemic therapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Investigator-assessed overall objective disease response rate (ORR = CR + PR); secondary endpoint duration of response
pivotal_trials.result: ORR 34% (CR + PR; 33/96), 95% CI [25, 45]; CR 6% (6/96); PR 28% (27/96); median duration of response 15 months

nct_ctgov.title: A Single Agent Phase II Study of Romidepsin (Depsipeptide, FK228) in the Treatment of Cutaneous T-cell Lymphoma (CTCL)

pivotal_trials.trial_name: NCI 1312 (Study 2), the supportive single-arm phase II study
pivotal_trials.design: International, multicenter, non-randomized, single-arm, open-label study (CTCL arms)
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with a primary diagnosis of CTCL who received at least 2 prior skin directed therapies or one or more prior systemic therapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Investigator-assessed overall objective disease response rate (ORR = CR + PR); secondary endpoint duration of response
pivotal_trials.result: ORR 35% (CR + PR; 25/71), 95% CI [25, 49]; CR 6% (4/71); PR 30% (21/71); median duration of response 11 months

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (Study 1 / Study 2): nausea (56% / 86%), fatigue/asthenia (53% / 77%), infections (46% / 54%), vomiting (34% / 52%), anorexia (23% / 54%). Warnings include QT prolongation/ECG changes and hematologic toxicities (thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, anemia). Discontinuation due to AE occurred in 21% (Study 1) and 11% (Study 2).
target_moa: Romidepsin is a histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitor; it causes accumulation of acetylated histones and induces cell cycle arrest and apoptosis of some cancer cell lines

advisory_committee.vote: ODAC convened September 2, 2009; the committee concluded the two single-arm studies represented a favorable risk-benefit profile for patients with previously treated CTCL (no numeric vote tally stated in reviewed documents)

description.text: Added new indication for treatment of peripheral T-cell lymphoma (PTCL) in patients who have received at least one prior therapy (accelerated approval)

citations.quote: This “Prior Approval” supplemental new drug application proposes a new indication, for the treatment of peripheral T-cell lymphoma (PTCL) in patients who have received at least one prior therapy.

description.text: Voluntarily withdrew the accelerated-approval peripheral T-cell lymphoma (PTCL) indication

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for revisions to the US Prescribing Information to voluntarily remove the peripheral T-cell lymphoma (PTCL) indication, previously approved under accelerated approval under NDA 022393 supplement 4 on June 16, 2011.

orphan_indication.text: Romidepsin received orphan drug designation; this drug product for this indication has an orphan drug designation

citations.quote: Because this drug product for this indication has an orphan drug designation, you are exempt from this requirement.
Orphan status was granted to romidepsin development under CFR316, subpart C.

summary.text: Standard-review NDA approved for CTCL after at least one prior systemic therapy on the basis of two single-arm phase II studies (GPI-04-0001 and NCI 1312); the product had orphan drug designation and was discussed at an ODAC meeting on September 2, 2009.

citations.quote: The risk benefit analysis to support this recommendation was based on the efficacy and safety results of two multicenter, single arm clinical trials, GPI-04-0001, (GPI Study) and NCI1312, (NCI Study) in patients with CTCL.
Because this drug product for this indication has an orphan drug designation, you are exempt from this requirement.
The romidepsin efficacy and safety results were presented to the Oncology Drug Advisory Committee (ODAC) on September 2, 2009.

citations.quote: 1556-1 Conduct a GLP embryo-fetal developmental reproductive toxicology study in rats to assess the embryo-fetal toxicity of romidepsin. The results from the rat study will determine if a study in a second species is warranted.
